transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-21
Start: 15:23 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lina (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood SE), Maya (HydraWell Head of ML), Rajiv (Infra), Elena (Product), Tom (Finance)

Summary:
High-level: Discovery / POC scoping focused on unit economics and benchmark plan. Customer running a mix of short-context chat assistants (avg tokens: 90) and a document summarization path (avg tokens: 1,200) with sporadic longer extraction jobs. Main constraints: strict monthly budget, need SLOs for 95th perc latency <200ms for chat path, and ability to cap spend per feature. Wants cost model that shows per-token + batching/caching impact and an initial benchmark plan.

Topics discussed:
- Workload breakdown (chat vs summarization vs extraction)
- Target QPS/Worst-case concurrency and burst patterns
- Success criteria for POC (latency SLOs, cost per 1M tokens, accuracy baseline)
- Benchmark methodology and sample traces
- Deployment options: hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC
- Security/compliance checks (SOC2, audit logs, KMS)

Action items (recap at end): see metadata above

Transcript body:
00:00 Samir: all right everyone uh thanks for joining, we're gonna kick off on the cost and bench piece for the pilot, um quick intros?
00:07 Maya: yeah Maya here, head of ML at HydraWell, excited to get this scoped, we've got a pretty tight budget runway so want clarity on unit econs
00:14 Rajiv: Rajiv infra, we'll own the trace and run the benchmark VM's, also want to understand dedicated requirements
00:22 Samir: perfect, Lina do you wanna run through the typical measurements we collect?
00:26 Lina: sure, so we usually gather token-level timing, end-to-end latency from client to response, and GPU utilization plus memory peaks. for cost modeling we combine per-token compute cost with infra amortized + network. there's often savings from batching and prefix KV cache for repeated contexts.
00:45 Elena: can you say a bit more about the cache? how much savings do folks typically see?
00:50 Lina: yeah so that depends a lot on hit-rate. with a conversational assistant with stable system prompts we often see 20-40% token reduction from prefix cache re-use, sometimes higher if you have lots of repeated contexts. batching helps throughput but can add latency if you need 95th percentile tight.
01:07 Tom: from finance perspective we need a per-feature cap, like show me cost per 1M tokens for chat and cost per 1M tokens for summarization, and also illustrate best/worst-case month.
01:19 Samir: ok we'll produce a sheet with base-case per-token for the model variants you choose, and then run sensitivity for batching size, cache hit-rate, and quantization (if applicable).
01:31 Maya: our current mix is roughly 70% chat small interactions (avg 90 tokens), 20% summarization (avg 1,200 tokens), 10% long extraction (avg 5k tokens but only a few hundred calls/day). Peak concurrent chat QPS is around 220, average sustained 60.
01:47 Lina: good, that distribution matters a lot. for the chat path latency SLO of 95th <200ms, we need to decide if that maps to hosted low-latency tier or dedicated pinned capacity. often we recommend dedicated for stable high QPS to guarantee latency.
02:05 Rajiv: what GPU type are you modeling on? we run some on GCP A2 and also have access to private infra with A100. our ops preference is to avoid introducing hardware ops if we can stay on hosted.
02:18 Lina: in our cost model we provide variants: hosted inference w/ latency tier, dedicated on A100, and private (on-prem) estimate. A100 gives better throughput per dollar for large summarization jobs, but dedicated costs include reserved capacity commitment.
02:33 Samir: question for Maya on accuracy baseline — what delta vs current model is acceptable during pilot?
02:38 Maya: for chat we need parity or +2% improvement on NPS signals; for summarization we accept slight drop (up to 3%) if cost savings are >20%.
02:47 Diego: noted — we'll include accuracy guardrails in bench, run our eval harness against your labeled prompt set, and include MRR/ROUGE metrics.
02:56 Elena: timeline, how quickly can Redwood stand up benchmarks if we hand over traces?
03:01 Samir: if we get the 48-hour traces and a creds/access for a staging cluster, Lina's team can run a baseline within 5 business days, and we'll have cost model drafts in 3 business days after that inputs. so roughly 8 business days to a first delivery.
03:19 Tom: finance needs a runway scenario out to 6 months with high/low usage — can you provide both committed-cost and burst-cost views?
03:26 Samir: yes, we'll model committed vs burst: committed = reserved dedicated monthly + baseline usage; burst = hosted or autoscaling costs when above reserved. we'll put a waterfall chart in the sheet.
03:36 Maya: any gotchas on tokenization differences across models when comparing per-token cost?
03:41 Lina: good point. tokenization variance matters — we'll normalize to utf-8 byte-level tokenization and report tokens-per-request for each model. we'll also include an apples-to-apples measurement by running the same client payloads through the models.
03:53 Rajiv: security — we have to see SOC2, SAML SSO, audit logs and KMS behavior; will that delay the pilot?
03:59 Samir: not usually, we have SOC2 docs and an enterprise compliance pack; private deployments take longer but we can test hosted with strict data retention and optional bring-your-own-key (BYOK) for the pilot. we'll attach security docs in the follow-up.
04:13 Elena: for benchmarks, do you need real PII or can we obfuscate?
04:17 Rajiv: we prefer obfuscated but structurally identical traces, we'll scrub PII then send.
04:22 Lina: that's fine — model perf shouldn't shift much with obfuscation of named entities. just keep token lengths and punctuation similar.
04:29 Samir: ok let's walk through a sample benchmark plan — Lina?
04:32 Lina: step 1: ingest 48hr traffic, synthesize steady-state QPS and burst windows; step 2: run single-request latency and end-to-end across models; step 3: run batching sensitivity sweep (batch sizes 1, 4, 8, 16) and measure p50/p95 latency and throughput; step 4: measure prefix cache hit scenarios (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%) on chat; step 5: long-tail summarization throughputs on dedicated. we'll capture GPU util, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens.
05:10 Maya: can you quantify expected per-token ranges? even rough ballpark is helpful now.
05:14 Samir: sure approximate ranges: hosted small model in low-latency tier ~ $0.003 - $0.01 per 1k tokens depending on size and region; dedicated amortized can be lower for heavy summarization loads, maybe $0.001 - $0.005 per 1k tokens after commitment; but again those are variable. we'll include model-specific rows in the sheet.
05:34 Tom: hmm those ranges are broad — finance will want scenarios.
05:36 Lina: we'll run sensitivity for cache hit-rate and batching — example: chat path with 40% cache hit and batch size 4 might drop effective tokens billed by ~30% and lower per-token compute by 20-30%. but batching beyond what's tolerated by latency SLO will be a tradeoff.
05:56 Maya: if we need 95th <200ms we probably can't batch aggressively at peak, so we want to see per-second samples where burst QPS=220 and latency remains within SLO.
06:08 Lina: we'll include a 'latency guard' configuration that simulates strict SLOs and disables batch windows above X latency. that will show worst-case spend.
06:18 Rajiv: related — do you support KV cache sharing across replicas? we have multiple frontends for HA and want cache coherent behavior.
06:25 Diego: yes, Redwood runtime supports prefix KV cache at routing layer with configurable TTL and can be configured to be regional or per-replica; we'll note cache consistency modes in the runbook.
06:37 Elena: regarding deployment — if hosted doesn't meet latency we may consider dedicated; what's typical procurement lead time for dedicated?
06:43 Samir: committed dedicated often needs 2-4 weeks for capacity provisioning depending on GPU type and region. for pilot we can start on hosted low-latency tier and then migrate to dedicated once we agree on sizing.
06:55 Tom: any licensing or minimums we should know about?
06:58 Samir: for dedicated there's a monthly reservation; pilot discounts available for initial 3 months. we'll include a sample TCO with and without pilot discount.
07:08 Maya: ok hypotheticals — show me worst-case monthly cost for chat if we lose cache (0% hit) and traffic doubles.
07:14 Lina: we'll include that as a stress scenario: 0% cache + 2x qps = high spend scenario. also we'll show quantization options — int8/4bit can reduce runtime cost but sometimes affect quality; we'll quantify observed delta from prior tests.
07:30 Rajiv: for benchmarking infra, do you need SSH to our staging or will you spin workloads from your side?
07:35 Samir: prefer you run a lightweight runner we provide in staging to avoid network egress and to mirror your network latencies; we'll provide a docker runner and a step-by-step runbook.
07:44 Maya: acceptable. we'll get that staged.
07:46 Samir: timeline recap: traces by 2026-07-26, runner in staging by 2026-07-27, bench run and initial report by 2026-08-03, cost model and sensitivity sheets by 2026-08-05.
07:59 Elena: good. can you include a simple viz that maps latency vs batch size vs cost so product can pick operating point?
08:05 Lina: yes we'll produce a decision matrix with recommended knobs: batch size, cache TTL, quantization profile, and deployment type.
08:12 Tom: last question — competitors. we did a short evaluation of LatencyCloud and Anthropic earlier; how is Redwood different regarding unit econs?
08:20 Samir: Redwood focuses on controllability and tooling to tune batching/caching across deployments and shows the unit econs transparently; we'll demonstrate empirical numbers so you can compare. we'll also provide a competitor mapping doc.
08:33 Maya: okay, thanks. quick housekeeping — who owns follow-ups?
08:37 Samir: Samir will send initial cost workbook, Lina will send bench template and runbook, Rajiv to share traces. we'll set up infra call for July 28.
08:46 Elena: thanks everyone, sounds good.

(End of meeting)
